title.zh: 授权菲律宾总统接受国际货币基金组织协定条款修正案，以设立特别提款权机制并使该基金现行规则与做法的特定修改生效
title.en: An Act Authorizing the President of the Philippines to Accept the Amendment to the Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund So as to Establish a Facility for Special Drawing Rights and Giving Effect to Certain Modifications in the Present Rules and Practices of the Fund
title.orig: An Act Authorizing the President of the Philippines to Accept the Amendment to the Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund So as to Establish a Facility for Special Drawing Rights and Giving Effect to Certain Modifications in the Present Rules and Practices of the Fund

source.name: LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation）

completenessNote: 全文，共 5 条；逐字取自 LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation） 官方页面（statutes/repacts/ra1969/ra_6045_1969.html），未改写、未摘译、未节选；原文语言：英语。 条文抬头依源文为 “Section N.” 等形式，本库统一规范为 “Section N.”；首行抬头与条内标题的分段依源文块级边界还原。

text.en: This Act shall be cited as the "Special Drawing Rights Act."

The President of the Philippines is hereby authorized to accept the amendment to the Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund, hereinafter referred to as the "Fund," attached to the April 1968 Report of the Executive Directors to the Board of Governors of the Fund, for the purpose of (a) establishing a facility for Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) in the Fund and, (b) giving effect to certain modifications in the present rules and practices of the Fund.

The Central Bank of the Philippines is hereby authorized to receive and hold special drawing rights as may be allowed by the Fund and do all such acts as may be necessary to carry out the obligations of a participant m the Special Drawing Account of the Fund as may be prescribed by the Articles of Agreement of the Fund and the rules that may be duly promulgated thereunder.
All laws or parts of laws inconsistent with the provisions of this Act are hereby repealed.

This Act shall take effect upon its approval.
Approved, August 4, 1969.
